rubric.role_summary: Research data engineer building scalable data pipelines, storage and processing systems for multimodal scientific datasets used in analysis and machine-learning model training.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Research data engineer building scalable data pipelines, storage and processing systems for multimodal scientific datasets used in analysis and machine-learning model training.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative discipline AND significant industry experience in data engineering, MLOps, or data platform roles.
- Python engineering experience.
- Experience with cloud-native data infrastructure, such as AWS S3 or GCS.
- Experience designing data pipelines.
- Experience building analytical data processing workflows using modern engines or frameworks.
- Hands-on experience with workflow orchestration tools.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Experience with biomedical or genomics data, regulated or pharma-partnered environments, data governance, FAIR principles or research data management, or feature store implementations.
- Excellent Python engineering skills.
- Deep experience with cloud-native data infrastructure, such as AWS S3 or GCS and its surrounding ecosystem, AND infrastructure-as-code such as Terraform or equivalent.
- A track record of designing data pipelines and storage layouts for large, heterogeneous datasets.
- Experience building scalable analytical data processing workflows using modern engines or frameworks, with an understanding of their performance and architectural trade-offs.
- Hands-on experience with workflow orchestration AND containerised environments; listed tools are examples, not individually required.
- Working knowledge of modern columnar or scientific data formats AND lakehouse technologies; the listed formats are not individually required.
- Experience partnering closely with scientific or research users.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): Greater London area. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them.
